chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Erase the Book of Allah, the Exalted, and His remembrance with the cleanest substance you can find,' and he forbade burning the Book of Allah, and forbade erasing it with pens.

key_terms.ذِكْرَهُ: His remembrance (referring to the Quranic text)

ai.seo_question: How should written copies of the Quran be disposed of according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the preferred method for disposing of Quranic manuscripts by erasing the ink with a pure substance, thereby preserving the sanctity of the written word without the finality of burning. It specifically prohibits using pens for dry erasure, a detail that reflects the material culture of early Islamic manuscripts and underscores the reverence for the physical vessel of revelation. This practice highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on treating the Quran's text with both physical care and ritual purity.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘(You can) delete the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted and His<sup>azwj</sup> Mention with the cleanest of what you can find’, and he<sup>saww</sup> forbade to burn the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and forbade from deleting with the pens’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘You may delete (writing of) the book of Allah, the Most High and words mentioning Him with the cleanest thing that you can find.’ He prohibited the burning of the book of Allah and to delete it with a pen.’”
